title: Impact of Covenant Violations on Capital Expenditure

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).
- Why: Treatment assignment (treated = 1 if the firm is above the covenant debt-to-asset threshold) is determined by a running variable (debt-to-asset ratio). Firms just above vs. just below the threshold are plausibly comparable, enabling identification of the causal jump in log capex at the cutoff.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of log capex as a function of the debt-to-asset ratio is continuous at the threshold.
  - No precise manipulation: Firms cannot precisely sort around the covenant threshold to manipulate treatment status.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load data and implement a sharp RDD for the effect of crossing the covenant threshold on log capex.
# Includes: data-driven cutoff recovery, local linear RDD with triangular kernel,
# bandwidth sensitivity, higher-order polynomial, donut-hole, placebo cutoffs,
# and a near-cutoff OLS check using the provided near_cutoff flag.

# ---- 0) Setup ----
suppressWarnings({
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    # Base packages used; no external dependencies strictly required.
  })
})

# ---- 1) Read data ----
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s98_data.csv")

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("running_var","treated","y") %in% names(df)))

# ---- 2) Recover the cutoff (c_hat) from data ----
# Use empirical boundary between control and treated groups: midpoint between
# max running_var among controls and min running_var among treated.
rv <- df$running_var
treat_obs <- df$treated

min_treated <- suppressWarnings(min(rv[treat_obs == 1], na.rm = TRUE))
max_control <- suppressWarnings(max(rv[treat_obs == 0], na.rm = TRUE))

if (!is.finite(min_treated) || !is.finite(max_control)) {
  # Fallback: use the value minimizing misclassification on a grid
  grid <- quantile(rv, probs = seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.005), na.rm = TRUE, type = 7)
  miscl <- sapply(grid, function(cut) mean(as.integer(rv >= cut) != treat_obs))
  c_hat <- grid[which.min(miscl)]
} else {
  c_hat <- (min_treated + max_control) / 2
}

# Misclassification of observed treated vs threshold rule (diagnostic)
pred_treat <- as.integer(rv >= c_hat)
misclass_rate <- mean(pred_treat != treat_obs)

cat("Estimated cutoff (c_hat): ", round(c_hat, 4), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Misclassification rate of 'treated' vs rule 1[rv >= c_hat]: ",
    sprintf("%.2f", 100*misclass_rate), "%\n\n", sep = "")

# ---- 3) Local linear RDD estimator (triangular kernel) ----
rd_local_linear <- function(data, cutoff, h, p = 1, donut = 0) {
  x <- data$running_var - cutoff
  y <- data$y
  # Define treatment per RDD rule relative to cutoff (ensures internal consistency)
  t_local <- as.integer(x >= 0)

  # Sample within bandwidth and apply donut hole
  idx <- which(abs(x) <= h & abs(x) >= donut & is.finite(y) & is.finite(x))
  if (length(idx) < 20 || sum(x[idx] < 0) < 10 || sum(x[idx] >= 0) < 10) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, N = length(idx), N_left = sum(x[idx] < 0), N_right = sum(x[idx] >= 0)))
  }

  xw <- x[idx]
  yw <- y[idx]
  tw <- t_local[idx]

  # Triangular kernel weights
  w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(xw)/h)

  # Polynomial terms: allow different slopes each side via interactions
  df_reg <- data.frame(y = yw, t = tw, x = xw)
  if (p >= 2) {
    df_reg$x2 <- xw^2
  }

  # Model specification:
  # y = alpha + tau*t + b1*x + b2*t*x [+ b3*x^2 + b4*t*x^2] + e
  if (p == 1) {
    fit <- lm(y ~ t + x + t:x, data = df_reg, weights = w)
    coefs <- summary(fit)$coefficients
    tau <- coefs["t", "Estimate"]
    se  <- coefs["t", "Std. Error"]
  } else {
    fit <- lm(y ~ t + x + t:x + x2 + t:x2, data = df_reg, weights = w)
    coefs <- summary(fit)$coefficients
    tau <- coefs["t", "Estimate"]
    se  <- coefs["t", "Std. Error"]
  }

  list(tau = as.numeric(tau),
       se  = as.numeric(se),
       N = length(idx),
       N_left = sum(xw < 0),
       N_right = sum(xw >= 0))
}

# ---- 4) Choose bandwidths and run main estimate ----
rng <- diff(range(rv, na.rm = TRUE))
# Candidate bandwidths as fractions of the running variable range
cand_h <- sort(unique(pmax(pmin(c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2) * ifelse(is.finite(rng) && rng > 0, rng, 1), 0.5), 0.01)))

# Pick the smallest bandwidth with enough observations on both sides; else use the largest
res_list <- lapply(cand_h, function(h) rd_local_linear(df, c_hat, h = h, p = 1, donut = 0))
ok <- sapply(res_list, function(r) is.finite(r$tau) && !is.na(r$tau))
if (any(ok)) {
  h_main <- cand_h[which(ok)[1]]
  res_main <- res_list[[which(ok)[1]]]
} else {
  # Force use of the largest bandwidth to get an estimate (may still be NA if data are too sparse)
  h_main <- tail(cand_h, 1)
  res_main <- rd_local_linear(df, c_hat, h = h_main, p = 1, donut = 0)
}

cat("Main RD (local linear, triangular kernel)\n")
cat("  Bandwidth h = ", round(h_main, 4), "\n", sep = "")
cat("  Tau (log capex jump at cutoff) = ", round(res_main$tau, 4),
    "  [SE = ", round(res_main$se, 4), "]\n", sep = "")
if (is.finite(res_main$tau)) {
  pct <- 100 * (exp(res_main$tau) - 1)
  cat("  Interpreted as approx. ", sprintf("%.1f", pct), "% change in capex at threshold\n", sep = "")
}
cat("  N_left = ", res_main$N_left, ", N_right = ", res_main$N_right, ", N_total = ", res_main$N, "\n\n", sep = "")

# ---- 5) Robustness: bandwidth sensitivity ----
cat("Bandwidth sensitivity (p = 1):\n")
for (h in cand_h) {
  r <- rd_local_linear(df, c_hat, h = h, p = 1, donut = 0)
  cat("  h = ", format(round(h, 4), nsmall = 4),
      ": tau = ", ifelse(is.na(r$tau), "NA", round(r$tau, 4)),
      " [SE = ", ifelse(is.na(r$se), "NA", round(r$se, 4)), "]",
      " | N_left = ", r$N_left, ", N_right = ", r$N_right, "\n", sep = "")
}
cat("\n")

# ---- 6) Robustness: higher-order polynomial (quadratic) ----
res_p2 <- rd_local_linear(df, c_hat, h = h_main, p = 2, donut = 0)
cat("Quadratic specification (same h = ", round(h_main, 4), "):\n", sep = "")
cat("  tau = ", round(res_p2$tau, 4), " [SE = ", round(res_p2$se, 4), "]\n\n", sep = "")

# ---- 7) Robustness: donut hole (drop closest observations) ----
donut_w <- 0.01 * ifelse(is.finite(rng) && rng > 0, rng, 1)
res_donut <- rd_local_linear(df, c_hat, h = h_main, p = 1, donut = donut_w)
cat("Donut-hole (exclude |x| < ", round(donut_w, 4), ", h = ", round(h_main, 4), "):\n", sep = "")
cat("  tau = ", round(res_donut$tau, 4), " [SE = ", round(res_donut$se, 4), "]",
    " | N_left = ", res_donut$N_left, ", N_right = ", res_donut$N_right, "\n\n", sep = "")

# ---- 8) Robustness: placebo cutoffs ----
# Use +/- 10% of range, clipped to interior
shift <- 0.1 * ifelse(is.finite(rng) && rng > 0, rng, 1)
candidates <- c(c_hat - shift, c_hat + shift)
lo <- min(rv, na.rm = TRUE); hi <- max(rv, na.rm = TRUE)
candidates <- pmin(pmax(candidates, lo + 0.02 * (hi - lo)), hi - 0.02 * (hi - lo))

cat("Placebo cutoffs (local linear, p = 1, h = ", round(h_main, 4), "):\n", sep = "")
for (cp in candidates) {
  rpb <- rd_local_linear(df, cp, h = h_main, p = 1, donut = 0)
  cat("  c = ", round(cp, 4), ": tau = ", ifelse(is.na(rpb$tau), "NA", round(rpb$tau, 4)),
      " [SE = ", ifelse(is.na(rpb$se), "NA", round(rpb$se, 4)), "]",
      " | N_left = ", rpb$N_left, ", N_right = ", rpb$N_right, "\n", sep = "")
}
cat("\n")

# ---- 9) Near-cutoff OLS check using provided near_cutoff flag ----
if ("near_cutoff" %in% names(df)) {
  sub <- subset(df, near_cutoff == 1 & is.finite(y) & is.finite(running_var))
  if (nrow(sub) >= 30 && length(unique(sub$treated)) > 1) {
    ols1 <- lm(y ~ treated, data = sub)
    ols2 <- lm(y ~ treated + running_var, data = sub)
    s1 <- summary(ols1)$coefficients
    s2 <- summary(ols2)$coefficients
    cat("Near-cutoff OLS (near_cutoff == 1):\n")
    cat("  y ~ treated:  coef(treated) = ", round(s1["treated", "Estimate"], 4),
        " [SE = ", round(s1["treated", "Std. Error"], 4), "], N = ", nrow(sub), "\n", sep = "")
    cat("  y ~ treated + running_var:  coef(treated) = ", round(s2["treated", "Estimate"], 4),
        " [SE = ", round(s2["treated", "Std. Error"], 4), "], N = ", nrow(sub), "\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("Near-cutoff OLS: insufficient variation or sample size in near_cutoff == 1 subset.\n\n")
  }
}

# ---- 10) Final numeric result (main estimate) ----
if (is.finite(res_main$tau)) {
  cat("Final (main) RD estimate: tau = ", round(res_main$tau, 4),
      " (log points). Approximate percent change = ",
      sprintf("%.1f", 100*(exp(res_main$tau)-1)), "%\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("Final (main) RD estimate not available due to insufficient support within bandwidth.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Crossing above the covenant threshold (treated = 1) should tighten lender control and reduce investment outlays, leading to a drop in log capex at the cutoff.
- Magnitude: A decrease of roughly 10–20% in capex is plausible (tau ≈ −0.10 to −0.22 in log terms), consistent with the literature on covenant violations constraining investment. Robustness checks should show a stable negative jump across reasonable bandwidths and specifications, with no systematic effects at placebo cutoffs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the discontinuity at the covenant threshold to identify causal effects.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the covenant threshold leads to a significant increase in capital expenditure.
